key_insight: MedHarnessBench shows that healthcare-specific runtime support can improve agent task success and reveal process failures that terminal outcomes miss.
clinical_relevance: For healthcare AI systems, evaluating how agents use tools, follow workflows, and respect boundaries is crucial for safer, more reliable deployment.
method: Defined the Medical Harness Protocol to score seven healthcare process dimensions.
Built MedHarnessBench with 342 executable tasks spanning FHIR/EHR, admin interfaces, and multimodal clinical tools.
Ran more than 16,000 controlled executions and compared against general-purpose harnesses with single-fault perturbations.
evidence_signal: The benchmark reports broad gains in terminal success, subtask completion, and process quality across over 16,000 controlled task executions.
watch_item: Results come from benchmarked executions, so real-world performance may differ when tools, data quality, and clinical workflows are less controlled.
paper_title: MedHarnessBench: A Unified Benchmark for Healthcare Agent Evaluation
